extracted.intended_audience: Users/developers of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational commutative algebraists) who use the multigrading and modular-walk libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation and usage guidelines for SINGULAR library procedures (multigrading.lib and modwalk.lib) describing purpose, usage, parameters, return values, notes and examples for attaching multigradings and computing Groebner/standard bases by modular methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: modfrWalk (modwalk.lib)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: a standard basis of I. The procedure computes a standard basis of I (over the rational numbers) by using modular methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage examples: LIB "modwalk.lib"; prepare ring and ideal, compute I = std(I); fetch the ideal into the target ring, choose an int radius argument and call modfrWalk(I, radius) (optionally with ordering or weight vector: modfrWalk(I,radius,"Dp") or modfrWalk(I,radius,"Dp",w)). The procedure returns a standard basis (examples in the manual show several returned J[i] polynomials). Note: the input I is assumed to be a Groebner basis in the source ordering before calling modfrWalk; the procedure uses modular techniques and works over Q. Example shows computing standard bases for univariate and multivariate examples and a variant with weight vector w = 3,2,1,2.

rubrics_metrics.name: multigrading.lib (overview / purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Multigraded Rings. This library allows one to virtually add multigradings to Singular: grade multivariate polynomial rings with arbitrary (finitely generated Abelian) groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview includes references (E. Miller & B. Sturmfels; M. Kreuzer & L. Robbiano) and a link to the convext-singular wiki for more. The library supports attaching weight matrices and grading groups to the base ring and provides procedures to query and manipulate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegBasis external dependency (note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: 'multiDegBasis' relies on 4ti2 for computing Hilbert Bases. All groups are finitely generated Abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for users: installation/availability of 4ti2 is required for parts of the library (multiDegBasis) that compute Hilbert bases; ensure 4ti2 is available/linked when using those features.

rubrics_metrics.name: setBaseMultigrading
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: setBaseMultigrading(M[, G]); M is an integer matrix, G is a group (or lattice). Purpose: attaches weights of variables and grading group to the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: M encodes the weights of variables column-wise. Return: nothing. Examples demonstrate: constructing weight matrix M and grading group L (integer matrices), calling setBaseMultigrading(M,L) attaches grading to the current basering; getVariableWeights(), getLattice(), getLattice("hermite") then return the attached data. The manual also shows uses with/without torsion and with different matrix shapes (e.g., M[3][3], L[3][2], M[2][3] with torsion L[2][1], and extreme cases). Tests in examples assert equality (getVariableWeights()==M etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: getVariableWeights
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getVariableWeights([R]). Purpose: get associated multigrading matrix for the basering [or R]. Return: intmat, matrix of multidegrees of variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show getVariableWeights() returns the matrix M previously attached via setBaseMultigrading. Tests include comparisons (getVariableWeights() == M) and usage with explicit ring argument and basering. Works for cases with torsion and different matrix sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: getGradingGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getGradingGroup([R]). Purpose: get associated grading group. Return: group, the grading group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: def G = getGradingGroup(); printGroup(G); The printed group includes 'Generators' and 'Relations' and the example asserts that the group's components correspond to the matrices M and L passed previously (G[1]==M; G[2]==L). Examples include cases with torsion and extreme cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: getLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: getLattice([R[,opt]]). Purpose: get associated grading group matrix, i.e. generators (cols) of the grading group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intmat, the grading group matrix, or its Hermite normal form if optional argument ("hermiteNormalForm" / "hermite") is given, or Smith normal form if optional arg ("smith") is given. Examples show getLattice() == L after setBaseMultigrading(M,L) and print(getLattice("hermite")) returning the Hermite normal form; examples also demonstrate behavior with torsion and extreme cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: createGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: createGroup(S, L); S, L are integer matrices. Purpose: create the group of the form (S+L)/L, i.e. S specifies generators, L specifies relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: group. Examples: createGroup(S,L) followed by printGroup(G) shows the group's Generators and Relations. Several example matrices illustrate various configurations (identity, torsion, etc.). The procedure is used to construct custom grading groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: createQuotientGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: createGroup(L); L is an integer matrix. Purpose: create the group of the form (I+L)/L, where I is the square identity matrix of size nrows(L) x nrows(L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: L specifies relations between free generators of Z^nrows(L). Return: group. Example: def G = createQuotientGroup(L) constructs Z^n / L as a shortcut. The manual also shows the equivalent general construction createGroup(I,L).

rubrics_metrics.name: createTorsionFreeGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: createTorsionFreeGroup(S); S is an integer matrix. Purpose: create the free subgroup generated by S within the free Abelian group of rank nrows(S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: group. Example block begins in the manual (example text truncated here) — intended to produce a torsion-free group generated by the given S matrix. Use when a torsion-free subgroup is required from given generators.
